questions.q: What are the two AI pilots already running at LTV Global when this lesson begins?
options: A generative-AI customer-service assistant trained on support tickets, and an ML demand-forecasting model trained on Atlas order data
A fraud-detection model and a chatbot for employee IT help desk tickets
Two separate forecasting models, one for Atlas and one for Harbor
No AI pilots exist yet; this lesson only plans hypothetical future use cases
questions.explain: The lesson introduces a generative-AI support assistant (trained on Beacon/Comet tickets) and an ML demand-forecasting model (trained on Atlas order history) as pilots already underway before governance caught up.

questions.q: What are the five checks in Marcus Ibe's AI governance checklist?
options: Budget, headcount, vendor contract, deployment date, and marketing plan
Risk tier, data provenance, bias and fairness, model documentation, and a monitoring plan
SQL syntax, index usage, query runtime, backup schedule, and disk space
Customer satisfaction score only
questions.explain: The lesson lists exactly these five checks, adapted from the career path's AI & Machine Learning Governance course.

questions.q: Why does the demand-forecasting model score a MODERATE risk tier rather than HIGH?
options: It is customer-facing and uses unscrubbed free-text data
It is internal-only and trains on structured CDEs (OrderTotal, SKU) that already have owners and a Lesson 7 quality gate behind them
It has no training data at all
Risk tiers are assigned randomly at LTV Global
questions.explain: The lesson explains the forecasting model inherits governance from already-owned, quality-checked CDEs, keeping its risk tier moderate and internal.

questions.q: Which checks does the support assistant's model card fail outright?
options: It passes every check with no issues
It only fails the monitoring plan check
No owner is named, its training data includes unscrubbed Confidential and DateOfBirth-adjacent fields, and no monitoring plan is defined
It fails only the risk-tier check
questions.explain: The lesson states the support assistant model card has no named owner, unscrubbed Confidential/DateOfBirth data in training, and no monitoring plan — three concrete failures.

questions.q: What governance requirement applies specifically to the support assistant before it can send replies autonomously?
options: None — it can launch immediately once trained
It must be retrained quarterly regardless of performance
A human must review every drafted reply before it is sent, given its HIGH risk tier
It must be moved from Beacon to Comet
questions.explain: The lesson specifies human-in-the-loop review of every drafted reply as a requirement for the HIGH-risk support assistant before it can operate without full human review.
